To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Zn isotopic composition of plants and soil is determined by chemical isotope effects upon complexation by malates, citrates, and phosphates, and that these isotope effects are calculated by ab initio quantum chemical methods.
the Zn isotopic composition of the various parts and compartments of a plant depends on the pH and on the chemical species in which Zn is complexed.
the Zn isotopic composition of plants and soils is determined by chemical isotope effects in aqueous malates, citrates, and phosphates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of stable isotope geochemistry to understand the behavior of trace elements in soils, sediments, and aquatic systems.
the application of stable Zn isotopes as a tracer of Zn availability in soils and of Zn mobility in the plant.
the development of new analytical methods and the application of these techniques to the study of trace elements in environmental samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isotopic composition of Zn in plant roots is controlled by Zn phosphate complexation and the isotopic composition in leaves is controlled by the complexation with Zn malates and/or citrates.
Zn isotope ratios are fractionated in plants, and the isotopic composition in the roots is controlled by Zn phosphates.
Zn isotope ratios are a promising new tool for studying Zn uptake, distribution and speciation in plants and soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Zn isotope fractionations are controlled by the Zn complexation in the plants.
the Zn isotopic composition in the soil is expected to be close to the isotopic composition of the groundwater.
the Zn isotope fractionations in plants are mainly controlled by the Zn speciation in the rhizosphere and by the Zn speciations in the leaves and roots of plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Zn isotopic composition of the various plant parts is determined by the Zn ligand in the plant cell, and that the Zn isotopes can be used to trace Zn mobility in soils.
the isotope composition of Zn can be used to trace the chemical forms of Zn in soils and plants.
the isotopic fractionation of Zn is controlled by the chemical speciation of Zn in the environment.
